bodies.thread:
Vector databases are currently experiencing a surge in popularity as the AI hype cycle reaches its peak.

These systems store data as high-dimensional vectors, which are mathematical representations of features or attributes.

The number of dimensions in these embeddings ranges from "a few hundred to tens of thousands".

To find semantically similar records, these databases typically implement approximate nearest neighbor algorithms.

Developers can also combine vector retrieval with metadata filtering or lexical search to support hybrid workflows.

In recent benchmarks, HNSW-based implementations have been among the best performers.

Retrieval-augmented generation is a common use-case for these systems to improve domain-specific responses of large language models.

Funding activity reflects this interest, with companies like Zilliz raising $60M and Chroma scoring $18 million in seed funding at a $75 million valuation.
